figs.cap: Square artificial spin ice. (a) Geometry of tiled four-moment vertices with lattice spacing a and nearest- and next-nearest neighbor interactions J_NN^dip and J_NNN^dip. (b) Energy hierarchy and multiplicity of single-vertex configurations Tᵢ (i=1… 4). (c) The double-vertex environment (light gray) acting on the central island (dark gray) determines the energy barrier for moment switching. (d,e) For reversal via coherent rotation a perpendicular magnetization M^⊥≠ 0 exerted by the environment can lift the degeneracy for clockwise and counter-clockwise reversal energy barriers.

Demagnetization behavior for different lattice parameters for (a-c) the mean-field barrier model and (d-f) the chiral-split-barrier model. Black lines show the time evolution of the net magnetization M_[11](t) of different kMC runs (left-handed vertical scales). Shaded areas (with values given on the right-handed scale) denote the population of T₃ vertices (red, in forefront) and T₂ vertices that do not align with the initial [11] direction, separated into rotated T₂^⊥ (cyan, from zero) and reversed T₂^[11] (blue, stacked on T₂^⊥ population). Insets on the right show representative spatial configurations of vertices at times where the net magnetization is at 75%, 50% and 25% of its initial value. Vertex color coding is equivalent to Fig. 1 (a).

Average time at which M_[11]=75% for the mean-field barrier model (blue squares) and the chiral-split-barrier model (red circles). For strong interactions (small a), the mean-field model shows slower evolution due to correlated string propagation, whereas the chiral-barrier model generally features faster kinetics due to the reduction of switching barriers. The effect of kinetic blocking via subsequent creation and annihilation of T₃ vertices in the chiral-barrier model is apparent by the upturn at low values of a, as strong interactions lead to pronounced barrier splitting. Both models approach each other at large lattice constants a.

Initial demagnetization steps. (a) Spin configuration after a first spin flip creating a T₃ pair. Distinct transitions are labeled with letters, and unmarked moments are of transition type B (T₂T₂→ T₃T₃, see Tab. 1 ). Transitions which are highly unlikely to occur are marked in light gray (e.g., transition D). (b,c) Transition probabilities pᵢ in dependence of the lattice parameter a for (b) mean-field barrier energies and (c) when taking into account additional chiral splitting of the barriers. The probability p_B/A (black dotted line) demarks the transition between demagnetization dominated via string propagation (transition A, blue) and creation of new T₃ pairs (B, red).
